title: [BugFix][Worker] Restore Gemma 4 KV cache capacity on Model Runner V2
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fixes #19259. Related report: #18941.

After #14872 (`fd815467c221ee600137f6bdd53fe354d5e7c999`), ordinary full/sliding attention groups use private per-layer allocations even though upstream vLLM's standardized planner budgets for overlapping groups in one physical pool. `_scale_kv_cache_memory_for_multi_group` compensates with `max(group page bytes) / sum(all group page bytes)`. Gemma 4 31B's 50 sliding + 10 full layers become six equal groups, reducing the advertised budget and block count to 1/6. The same six-group geometry occurs for 26B-A4B and E4B; E2B has five groups and a 1/5 factor. The issue includes source permalinks and before/after planner evidence.

This change restores physical sharing and removes the corresponding budget reduction together:

- Use one common eligibility check in the worker and V2 runner for dense full/sliding attention with equal physical page sizes.
- Materialize the planner's overlapping layer slots from one allocation. Each slot has separate contiguous K and V halves, retaining the layout required by PA while also supporting different full/SW head dimensions and block sizes.
- Groups share the scheduler block pool, where a live block ID belongs to one group at a time. Equal page sizes make each ID map to equal byte ranges across groups. Distinct live IDs therefore remain isolated even though their layer slots alias.
- Validate descriptors before allocation; never silently fall back to private buffers after advertising the full shared budget.

The new path is limited to FP16/BF16, symmetric dense K/V, unpadded pages, and layer/block-compact layouts without KV transfer or context parallelism. Other cache layouts retain their existing behavior. The eligibility gate is intentionally restricted to `gemma4_text` and standard dense cache dtypes to keep this fix local to the reported regression. Non-Gemma models retain their original paths, including the existing Step model exemptions. There is no new environment variable or runtime copy.

**Runner scope:** This PR now targets **Model Runner V2 only**. Ascend selects V2 by default unless explicitly overridden or a feature requires V1 fallback. V1 allocation code is unchanged, and the worker enables the new Gemma 4 budget exemption only when V2 is selected. Shared helpers live in `vllm_ascend/worker/v2/attn_utils.py`; no separate core helper module is added. Existing layout/quantization/transfer safety conditions remain in place. The previously reported A5/V2 hardware tests exercised the same shared allocation algorithm; the scope/helper relocation update has now passed both CPU CI lanes and the hardware CI jobs listed below. The four A2 jobs blocked during container initialization still need a successful run.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Compatible Gemma 4 full/sliding attention configurations using Model Runner V2 regain the shared-pool KV capacity instead of losing it to the five/six-group private-allocation factor. Quantized model weights are independent of this restriction; quantized **KV caches** retain their existing path. Release note: `release_notes/fragments/19264.yaml`.

### How was this patch tested?

Added `tests/ut/worker/test_full_sliding_kv_cache.py`:

- Five/six-group worker budget regression: V2 retains the full shared budget, while V1 and unsupported runners retain their original scaling. Existing Step exemptions are unchanged.
- V2 allocating a single backing pool, FP16/BF16, unequal head dimensions/block sizes with equal physical pages.
- Real PyTorch K/V writes after the production V2 reshape method, with multiple kernel block sizes, checking six-group isolation, slot separation, shared storage, contiguous views, and V2 shared-layer references.
- Uniform group wrappers, multi-layer descriptors, unsupported layouts, malformed descriptor failures before allocation, non-Gemma budget behavior, unchanged Step-3.5/3.7 exemptions, and partial model configurations used by existing tests.

Local validation on Windows/CPU:

- **56 passed** in an isolated harness using real PyTorch 2.10.0, the production helper, AST-extracted unchanged worker/runner method bodies, and upstream KV spec/dataclass definitions from the verified vLLM pin `a98247ab4db686ee03c66d5feb3c761e52a2f8ab`. NPU-dependent module initialization was bypassed; this is not a full integration run.
- Running the same budget regressions against the pre-fix worker at `d606456c4eddf1eeddfffb2b52b70a80e0d4769b` gives the expected **2 failures / 30 passes**: 12,288 vs 61,440 (five groups), and 10,240 vs 61,440 (six groups). The fixed worker passes both; the V1 cases retain the original budget behavior.
- Ruff 0.14.0 check and format check pass for all three changed Python files; `git diff --check` passes.
- Normal `python -m pytest -q tests/ut/worker/test_full_sliding_kv_cache.py` is blocked during conftest import because vLLM is unavailable in the local Windows environment.
- Attempted the required `bash format.sh ci` for this update; the current local shell cannot find pre-commit. Direct Ruff checks pass, but the full local hook run is not claimed as passing; the latest remote pre-commit CI passed.

#### Real A5 hardware validation (reported by the deployment tester)

The deployment tester applied this PR's patch to Ascend commit `2581a69bc` and supplied the following measurements. These are real NPU results from that deployment, separate from the author's local CPU harness above. The application was reported as conflict-free and used the existing editable installation. The exact applied PR revision, vLLM runtime SHA, CANN/torch_npu versions, and full launch command were not included in the supplied report; the CI vLLM pin below must not be interpreted as the hardware environment's confirmed version.

Configuration: Gemma 4 31B, BF16, TP=2, A5 devices 4/5, Model Runner V2, `max_model_len=8192`, `max_num_batched_tokens=2496` with chunked prefill. Prefix caching was disabled for the initial regression tests and enabled for the separate prefix-cache validation.

**Capacity comparison, with unchanged launch parameters for the before/after patch runs:**

| Metric | 0.27.1rc1 baseline | `2581a69bc` without patch | `2581a69bc` + this PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Reported available KV cache memory | 41.56 GiB | 6.93 GiB | 41.58 GiB |
| Reported KV token capacity | Not recorded | 21,353 | 128,210 |
| Estimated concurrency at 8k context | Not recorded | 2.61x | 15.65x |

This restores approximately 6x capacity, consistent with eliminating the six-group budget factor. Startup, graph capture, and inference succeeded. The concurrency figures above are startup estimates, not measured simultaneous requests.

**Long-input isolation and cancellation/reuse:**

- Inputs were measured with `AutoTokenizer`: 5,632-5,650 tokens, cross-checked against API usage (example: 5,645 prompt tokens), above the 1,024-token sliding window. Input plus output stayed below 8,192 tokens.
- Serial baseline: 16/16 HTTP successes and 16/16 correct request-specific identifiers.
- Two rounds of 16 client-concurrent requests: 32/32 HTTP successes and 32/32 correct identifiers, with no observed cross-request leakage.
- Eight streaming requests were cancelled, followed by eight new requests: all eight replacement requests succeeded and returned their own identifiers. The service remained operational.
- Observed scheduler `Running` peaked at 5 in sampled logs; this does not establish 16 simultaneously resident requests or the maximum serving concurrency.
- Reported device memory rose from 80,662 MB to 80,842 MB (+180 MB) and remained at that level after the load, with no continuing growth during the approximately one-minute test. This is short-run evidence, not a long-term leak test.
- No ERROR, Traceback, OOM, illegal memory access, or worker exit was observed in the reported test window.

**Prefix caching enabled:**

| Test | HTTP success | Correct request-specific identifier |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1: initially cold cache, serial, shared 5,418-token prefix + 8 distinct suffix identifiers | 8/8 | 8/8 |
| R2: warm cache, serial, same prefix + 8 new identifiers | 8/8 | 8/8 |
| R3: warm cache, 8 client-concurrent requests, same prefix + 8 new identifiers | 8/8 | 8/8 |

- `prefix_cache_queries_total`: 0 -> 131,135; `prefix_cache_hits_total`: 0 -> 123,648. The aggregate hit ratio is **94.3%**, matching the service log's `Prefix cache hit rate: 94.3%`.
- No cross-request identifier leakage was observed in these 24 requests. The aggregate counters demonstrate cache reuse; they do not by themselves prove every shared-prefix token hit in every request.
- Available KV memory and token capacity remained **41.58 GiB / 128,210 tokens** with prefix caching enabled.
- No ERROR, OOM, or worker exit was reported.

The tester retained the initial regression JSON at `/workspace/logs/gpqa-regression-result.json`, test logs in the same directory, and 158 device-memory samples at `/tmp/gpqa-mem.log` on the test host. These are tester-local artifacts, not public download links.

**Remaining coverage (V2):** image/multimodal requests, retrieval of an identifier placed outside the sliding window (the tested identifiers were near the prompt end), sustained high-residency/block-pressure workloads, long-duration stability, other hardware/backend paths, and a formal accuracy/throughput benchmark. These results support the tested A5/V2 configuration, not all supported configurations.

**Previous CI at head e8c424dc65 (before descriptor-check simplification):** [Run 39540278263](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/39540278263).

- Passed: pre-commit, DCO, CPU UT against both the verified vLLM main pin and v0.31.0, all selected 310P and A3 partitions, A2 single-card partitions 3/4/5, and the selected upstream end-to-end job.
- A2 single-card partitions 1/2/6/7 failed in **Initialize containers**, before repository checkout or test execution. All four logs report containerd/runc failing to apply the cgroup CPU set: writing `0-191,+1-23` or `0-191,+24-46` to `cpuset.cpus` returns `invalid argument`. This is a runner/container startup failure; these jobs did not execute the PR code. [Example failed job](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/39540278263/job/119033522939).
- Consequently, the aggregate ci-gate is red. The runner configuration needs correction and the blocked jobs need rerunning before claiming a fully green CI run. A5 CI was skipped; the separately reported A5 hardware results above remain the available A5 evidence.

**Review follow-up at head 1e28169960:** Removed redundant descriptor checks for layer coverage, duplicates, offsets, bounds, and byte parity. The upstream default planner constructs coverage and offsets; dense symmetric FP16/BF16 pages guarantee even byte sizes. Retained shared-backing/positive-block and contiguous layer/block stride checks. The planner may round a block stride up for alignment, so an upstream-valid descriptor is not necessarily compatible with the contiguous K/V split.

Cross-checked the verified vLLM pin and latest vLLM main a9bf45ed8a856a0b1839197152d0d26fabb6599c. The latter moved placement into [kv_cache_planning.py](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/a9bf45ed8a856a0b1839197152d0d26fabb6599c/vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_planning.py#L569); alignment rounding and descriptor construction remain. Ascend main e5e820d5c935e6197bec8bc13e8e8936eb2740d0 still uses the same verified vLLM pin and has no intervening changes to the two modified production files. This source comparison does not claim runtime compatibility with unpinned vLLM main.

Gemma 4 remains the sole model gate; cache-format/layout/transfer exclusions are retained because model_type alone does not establish their compatibility. Local isolated CPU regression: 56 passed; Ruff and diff checks passed. Full local format.sh remains blocked by missing pre-commit. Fresh CI for this follow-up is pending.

The PR remains in draft pending remaining review and validation.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: Empty/single-type specs, offsets, multiple layers, invalid strides, and zero blocks.
- [x] **Regression test**: Five/six-group budget tests fail against the pre-fix worker.
- [x] **Error / failure path coverage**: Invalid descriptors fail before allocation.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: Storage aliasing and isolation checked by real tensor writes.
- [ ] **Performance impact**: A5/V2 capacity and targeted end-to-end regressions reported above; formal throughput benchmarking and broader hardware coverage remain pending.


- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/a98247ab4db686ee03c66d5feb3c761e52a2f8ab
